trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: This is the platinum, so it asks for everything else on the list rather than one trick of its own. Work the roadmap in order: finish the campaign in Phase 1, sweep the stranger strands and properties in Phase 2, grind the counted collectibles and activities in Phase 3, then close out 100 percent completion. Keep this tracker open as you play and tick each trophy off the moment it pops, because the platinum only lands once all 54 others are earned. There is no shortcut and no purchase that replaces the grind, so pace the long counts across several sessions.
trophies.sources: Official PlayStation trophy description; Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI PSN trophy list; PSNProfiles — GTA VI Trophy Guide

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: Play the opening mission, Gone Fishing, from a fresh start and simply see it through to the end. Treat it as your tutorial lap: learn the movement, driving and cover basics here, because later missions assume you know them. The trophy pops on completion, so there is nothing extra to collect inside the mission. If you skip a cutscene you still earn it, but watching the opener sets up the story threads the chapter trophies build on.
trophies.sources: Official PlayStation trophy description; Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI PSN trophy list

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: Finish every mission that makes up Chapter 1 and this unlocks as the chapter closes. Follow the main story markers only and resist detouring into the counted grinds yet, since the map and systems open up gradually. Any difficulty is fine because the description only asks for completion. Story progress can always be continued from your save, so this one cannot be locked out permanently.
trophies.sources: Official PlayStation trophy description; PSNProfiles — GTA VI Trophy Guide

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide: Complete Chapter 2 in full and the trophy lands with the chapter's final mission. By now both protagonists' routines are established, so use this chapter to learn switching between them under pressure. Keep a rolling manual save at each chapter boundary as insurance for the choice-based trophies later. Completion is all that matters here, not mission scores or speed.
trophies.sources: Official PlayStation trophy description; Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI PSN trophy list

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide: See Chapter 3 through to its last mission. The city districts and side systems are mostly open by this point, which makes it a good moment to start the vehicle discovery and exploration tallies in the background while you travel between story beats. Do not start the final push on counted collectibles yet; story first keeps the missable story moments in front of you. The trophy is awarded for finishing the chapter, however you play it.
trophies.sources: Official PlayStation trophy description; PSNProfiles — GTA VI Trophy Guide

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 4, the last full chapter before the endgame sequence. Before starting its final missions, top up ammo, armour and cash, and make a separate save slot you do not overwrite. That spare save is your safety net for any choice or event trophy tied to the finale. Once the chapter closes, move straight into the final mission while the mechanics are fresh.
trophies.sources: Official PlayStation trophy description; Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI PSN trophy list

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide: Complete the final story mission to earn this gold. Go in with full health supplies and your best vehicles and weapons prepared, and keep that pre-finale save from Chapter 4 untouched until the credits roll. If a choice is offered near the end, remember the separate save lets you return and see the other branch for the choice-based trophy. Finishing the mission also unlocks true free roam, which is when Phases 2 and 3 of the roadmap become fully available.
trophies.sources: Official PlayStation trophy description; PSNProfiles — GTA VI Trophy Guide; Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI PSN trophy list

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide: Finish the named mission Breakfast Run when it appears on your story path. It is a main mission rather than an optional job, so following the campaign markers leads you straight to it. Play it cleanly the first time and note any set-piece inside it, because several event trophies in this list are attached to specific missions. Completion alone earns the trophy; no medal or time target is mentioned in the description.
trophies.sources: Official PlayStation trophy description; Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI PSN trophy list

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide: Complete The Cartel Heist, the big set-piece robbery on the story path. Prepare like a heist deserves: full armour, a fast getaway vehicle staged where the plan allows, and a save made just before you start it. Heist missions are also where the bank and vault robbery trophies get their practice, so learn the escape routes here. The trophy needs the heist finished, not a perfect take.
trophies.sources: Official PlayStation trophy description; PSNProfiles — GTA VI Trophy Guide

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.guide: Finish the mission Child's Play when the campaign offers it. Keep following the main markers and it cannot be skipped over, since later chapters build on its outcome. If the mission contains a timed or escorted section, prioritise the objective over exploring; you can return to the area in free roam afterwards. The trophy pops on completion regardless of how messy the run was.
trophies.sources: Official PlayStation trophy description; Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI PSN trophy list

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.guide: Complete the mission Headliners as part of the main campaign. Treat any vehicle or on-foot chase inside it as practice for the race wins you will need later. As with the other named-mission trophies, there is no extra condition beyond finishing, so a straightforward clear is enough. Keep your chapter-boundary save habit going so a failed attempt never costs you progress elsewhere.
trophies.sources: Official PlayStation trophy description; PSNProfiles — GTA VI Trophy Guide

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.guide: Finish the mission VCIA Takedown, and while you are inside it, watch for the unscheduled departure moment that the Catch Me If You Can trophy describes, because that event belongs to the airport setting and cannot be staged the same way in free roam. The point of no return is the end of this mission: if you finish VCIA Takedown without making the unscheduled departure, reload your pre-mission save rather than hoping for a later chance. The completion trophy itself is safe either way, but pairing the two saves a replay. Keep a save from just before this mission until both are ticked off.
trophies.sources: Official PlayStation trophy description; Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI PSN trophy list

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.guide: Complete Operation Savage Glory on the story path. It reads as a heavy combat operation, so bring armour, snacks and your strongest weapons, and use Combat Focus deliberately here to practise lining up the five takedowns the Gunslinger trophy wants in a single use. Finishing the operation is the whole requirement. Afterwards, note the operation's area for the exploration tally, since story travel often leaves one district half revealed.
trophies.sources: Official PlayStation trophy description; PSNProfiles — GTA VI Trophy Guide

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: Reach a full 100 percent on the game's completion counter for this gold. The counter is fed by the same work the rest of the list demands: story, stranger strands, collectible sets, activity wins and property purchases, so use the in-game completion checklist as your ledger and this tracker as your second pair of eyes. Leave it until Phase 4, then hunt the last few percentage points category by category instead of wandering. When everything else in this guide is ticked, this one should be at or near the line; whatever remains is usually a partially finished counted set.
trophies.sources: Official PlayStation trophy description; Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI PSN trophy list; PSNProfiles — GTA VI Trophy Guide

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Land 250 stunts in total, tracked by the counter PlayStation shows for this trophy. The efficient pattern is to chain stunt opportunities while travelling between other objectives: ramps, jumps and airtime moments all feed the same tally, so a fast bike or light car becomes your default transport during Phase 3. Do short dedicated loops only for the final stretch, and check the counter every twenty or so stunts so a stalled session is spotted early. Because the total is large, starting casually during the story saves a painful endgame grind.
trophies.sources: Official PlayStation trophy description (count 250); Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI PSN trophy list

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Sample every activity type once; the starter data for this list counts 9 types. You do not need to win or even finish most of them, just start each one so the game registers the attempt. Work down the map's activity icons in one sweep during Phase 3 and tick them off as you go. This is also the perfect scouting run: you will see which activities feed the bigger trophies, like the races, the drone events and the shooting range, and can plan their grinds properly.
trophies.sources: Official PlayStation trophy description; PSNProfiles — GTA VI Trophy Guide

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Earn gold in all 42 Shooting Range challenges. Learn each weapon class on its early challenges first, because the later lanes assume fast target transitions and controlled bursts rather than spray. If a challenge keeps landing silver, change one variable at a time: sensitivity, weapon variant or firing rhythm. Golds are permanent once banked, so clear them range by range and use the tracker counter to confirm none were missed. Save this for Phase 3 when your combat skills from the campaign are sharp.
trophies.sources: Official PlayStation trophy description; Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI PSN trophy list (42 challenges)

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at all 14 locations. A win is needed, not just a finish, so fly each course once slowly to learn the gate order, then run it for real. Drone handling rewards smooth lines over raw speed; clipping a gate usually costs more time than a cautious corner. Mark each location off as its win lands, because with 14 venues the last two are easy to confuse. These races also sharpen the flying you will want for exploration clean-up.
trophies.sources: Official PlayStation trophy description; PSNProfiles — GTA VI Trophy Guide (14 locations)

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Win 20 different races; repeats of the same race do not grow the count, so variety is the whole game here. Pick the shortest or easiest event in each race family first and bank those wins early. Bring a vehicle suited to each class rather than forcing one favourite everywhere. Keep a written tally beside the tracker, because the trophy only cares about distinct wins and it is easy to double-race a favourite by accident.
trophies.sources: Official PlayStation trophy description; Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI PSN trophy list

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge. Find Cal's challenge through the fishing activity, learn the cast and reel timing on a practice round, then take the challenge seriously once the rhythm clicks. Fishing challenges usually reward patience over frantic input, so let the fish tire before reeling hard. If you lose, challenge him again straight away while the spot and timing are fresh in your hands.
trophies.sources: Official PlayStation trophy description; PSNProfiles — GTA VI Trophy Guide

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide: Complete one arcade game from start to finish. Any cabinet counts, so pick the shortest or simplest game you can find in an arcade or bar and see it through rather than sampling several. Completion is the requirement, not a high score, so play conservatively and protect your last life or credit. This pairs naturally with the Master of None sweep, since an arcade visit is one of the activity types to sample.
trophies.sources: Official PlayStation trophy description; Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI PSN trophy list

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Finish Andy's strand by completing his final mission. Stranger strands unlock in stages as the story advances, so if Andy's next job is not showing, push the campaign forward and check back. Do each strand to its end rather than juggling half-finished ones; the final mission only appears after the earlier ones are done. Andy is one of the strands that feeds the Strangers and Freaks count of eight, so closing his story helps two trophies at once.
trophies.sources: Official PlayStation trophy description; PSNProfiles — GTA VI Trophy Guide

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Complete Kenton's final mission to close his strand. The title hints the water is involved, so arrive with a boat or swim-friendly loadout if the job takes you off shore. As with every strand finale, the mission appears only after Kenton's earlier jobs are complete, so work his chain in order during Phase 2. Finishing counts toward the eight stranger strands the silver trophy tracks.
trophies.sources: Official PlayStation trophy description; Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI PSN trophy list

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Finish Billy's final mission. Expect riding or driving to feature, so bring a bike or vehicle you handle well and fuel it up before starting. Clear Billy's earlier strand missions first; the finale unlocks at the end of his chain. This is another of the eight strands counted by Strangers and Freaks, so Phase 2 is the time to close it alongside the other named characters.
trophies.sources: Official PlayStation trophy description; PSNProfiles — GTA VI Trophy Guide

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Complete 8 full stranger mission strands anywhere in Leonida for this silver. A strand means the whole chain for one character, from first meeting to final mission, not eight single jobs. The named finales in this list, for Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy and Tyrone, give you five strands; find three more from the stranger icons scattered across the state. Track strands, not missions, in your notes, and finish one character completely before starting the next to avoid confusion about which finale is still owed.
trophies.sources: Official PlayStation trophy description (8 strands); Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI PSN trophy list

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Complete Randy's final mission. A supply-themed strand usually means moving goods under pressure, so expect timed driving or defended deliveries and prepare a sturdy vehicle. Work Randy's chain from its first job; the finale only triggers once the earlier deliveries are done. Closing Randy out is one of the eight strands needed for the silver Strangers and Freaks trophy.
trophies.sources: Official PlayStation trophy description; PSNProfiles — GTA VI Trophy Guide

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Finish Tyrone's final mission to complete his strand. Keep progressing his earlier jobs whenever his icon is on the map, because strand finales are gated behind the whole chain. If a job involves showing off in a vehicle, practise the route once before committing to the scored attempt. Tyrone's finale is the fifth named strand in this list, leaving three more strands to find for the silver count of eight.
trophies.sources: Official PlayStation trophy description; Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI PSN trophy list

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at all 18 meditation spots spread across Leonida. Treat the spots like a collectible set: sweep the map region by region during Phase 3 and meditate at each one the moment you reach it, since a visited-but-not-used spot is the classic miss. Pair the hunt with the exploration trophy, because travelling to every spot reveals most of the 52 areas anyway. Keep a region checklist so the final spot is a known destination, not a state-wide guessing game.
trophies.sources: Official PlayStation trophy description; PSNProfiles — GTA VI Trophy Guide (18 spots)

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Hunt the unique animal Bret asks for. Accept Bret's request, track the animal using the clues or area the job gives you, and bring a weapon suited to a clean kill plus transport to reach wild country. Unique hunts are one-target jobs, so scout the area first instead of charging in and spooking it. Once the animal is down, finish the hand-in exactly as Bret directs so the strand registers the completion.
trophies.sources: Official PlayStation trophy description; Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI PSN trophy list

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.guide: Complete 3 full collectible card sets for this silver. Cards are found one at a time across Leonida, so the discipline is in the tracking: note which set each card belongs to and focus your searching on finishing sets rather than scattering effort across all of them. A set only counts when its last card is in hand, so prioritise the set closest to completion whenever you detour. Combine card hunting with the meditation and exploration sweeps so every trip serves two or three tallies at once.
trophies.sources: Official PlayStation trophy description (3 sets); PSNProfiles — GTA VI Trophy Guide

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.guide: Use the WAiNK interaction at 100 different locations for this silver. One hundred is the biggest location count on the list, so this is a route-planning trophy: work district by district, interact at every valid spot you pass, and never assume a location counted twice. The PlayStation counter is your referee, so check it after each district and re-sweep any area that under-delivered. Start sprinkling these in during the story so Phase 3 is finishing the tally, not starting it.
trophies.sources: Official PlayStation trophy description (100 locations); Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI PSN trophy list

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.guide: Complete 50 challenges of any kind. Challenges sit underneath most activities, so the fastest route is breadth: clear the easy challenges in races, ranges and stunt categories first rather than mastering one hard set. Keep a running count in this tracker and re-check which category is closest to its next completion whenever you sit down to play. Fifty sounds large, but steady progress during Phases 2 and 3 usually leaves only a small mop-up for the endgame.
trophies.sources: Official PlayStation trophy description (50 challenges); PSNProfiles — GTA VI Trophy Guide

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: While playing with your partner beside you, build a wanted level up to 4 stars, then lose it completely and escape. Deliberately set this up in a quiet area with a fast car and a planned hiding route, tunnels or off-road cover, rather than waiting for it to happen by accident. The key detail is the partner: the escape only counts with them present, so do not attempt it during solo errands. Once the stars clear and the escape registers, the trophy is yours.
trophies.sources: Official PlayStation trophy description; Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI PSN trophy list

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: With your partner, rob 3 shops in a row without your wanted level dropping off in between. Plan a tight triangle of shops in one district so travel time never lets the heat cool, and use one reliable getaway car for all three. The failure mode is escaping too well between shops, so stay visible enough to keep the wanted level alive while you move. If the chain breaks, restart the sequence from the first shop with the same route, it is short when rehearsed.
trophies.sources: Official PlayStation trophy description; PSNProfiles — GTA VI Trophy Guide

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.guide: Discover 100 different vehicles. Discovery comes from encountering and using vehicles across the state, so variety in your transport is the method: steal, borrow or buy something new whenever a model you have not driven crosses your path. Wealthy districts, marinas, airports and rural roads each hold models the others lack, which makes this a natural partner to the exploration sweep. The Scooter Bros registrations and garage purchases also put new vehicles in your hands, so combine all three tallies during Phase 3.
trophies.sources: Official PlayStation trophy description (100 vehicles); Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI PSN trophy list

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Take down 5 enemies during one single Combat Focus activation. Set it up rather than hoping for it: find a spot where at least five enemies cluster, such as a gang operation or a busy story shootout, weaken your approach so they group up, then trigger Combat Focus and work target to target without wasting shots. If you land four, do not panic-fire the last seconds away; reposition to a fresh cluster and try again with the lesson learned. Operation Savage Glory and the illegal operation robberies are reliable places to practise.
trophies.sources: Official PlayStation trophy description; PSNProfiles — GTA VI Trophy Guide

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA, the airport, meaning leave in a way the airport did not schedule: take an aircraft or vehicle and go. This is flagged missable because its natural moment sits inside the VCIA Takedown mission, and once that mission's airport sequence ends the scripted chance is gone. The point of no return is completing VCIA Takedown, so before finishing it, break away and depart the airport area on your own terms. If you already passed it, try departing from VCIA in free roam in an aircraft you were not assigned; if the trophy stays locked, the pre-mission save from the Hi-Jacked advice is the way back.
trophies.sources: Official PlayStation trophy description; Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI PSN trophy list

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.guide: This hidden trophy concerns the Rhino tanks: it gets kinda hot in them, so expect to deal with a Rhino directly, most likely during a story escalation or a military response. It is flagged missable because tank encounters tied to a mission set-piece do not repeat on demand; when a Rhino appears during the campaign, engage with it then, using heavy weapons or explosives from cover, instead of fleeing and assuming another will come. The point of no return is finishing the mission in which your Rhino encounter occurs. Keep a save before late-story missions so an armour-heavy replay is always available.
trophies.sources: Official PlayStation trophy description; PSNProfiles — GTA VI Trophy Guide

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store and get away without ever being detected. Scout the store first: note staff positions, cameras and the quickest exit, then enter quietly, control the room without raising an alarm and leave before attention builds. Detection is the only failure state, so a smaller, slower take beats a greedy one that trips an alarm. If you are spotted, let the attempt end and retry the same store with the layout fresh in your mind.
trophies.sources: Official PlayStation trophy description; Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI PSN trophy list

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.guide: Rob 5 bank vaults and escape each time for this silver. A vault robbery only counts when you both take the vault and get away, so plan the escape before you start the robbery: vehicle staged, route chosen, and a place to break line of sight. The Cartel Heist teaches the rhythm of a big job, so apply its lessons at smaller scale here. Space the five across Phase 3 so the wanted-level skills from Hot Together and Retail Therapy are fresh for each run.
trophies.sources: Official PlayStation trophy description (5 vaults); PSNProfiles — GTA VI Trophy Guide

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob an armoured truck and escape with the take. Armoured trucks need force or planning to open, so bring explosives or a heavy weapon and a fast car, and hit the truck somewhere your escape route is already clear. Guards respond quickly, so grab the money and move rather than fighting a growing response. Once you have broken away and the escape registers, the trophy lands; failed attempts cost nothing but time, so retry on the next truck you spot.
trophies.sources: Official PlayStation trophy description; Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI PSN trophy list

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.guide: Explore all of Leonida, which the list breaks into 52 areas. Exploration registers by travelling through each area, so systematic coverage beats fast highways: drive the local roads, cross the waterways and walk the odd shoreline. Combine this with the meditation spots, card hunting and WAiNK locations so one grand tour feeds four tallies. Near the end, compare your revealed map against the area count and hunt the blank patches, which are usually islands, swamps or a district corner the story never sent you to.
trophies.sources: Official PlayStation trophy description; PSNProfiles — GTA VI Trophy Guide (52 areas)

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob an illegal operation belonging to each gang; there are 9 gangs to cover. One operation per gang is enough, so the work is identification, not repetition: learn which operation belongs to whom before you hit it, and tick gangs off a written list. These robberies double as perfect Gunslinger practice, since operations hold clustered enemies. Vary your approach gang by gang, because an operation defended the same way as the last one still punishes a lazy entry.
trophies.sources: Official PlayStation trophy description; Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI PSN trophy list (9 gangs)

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach. This reads as a quiet story-adjacent moment rather than a challenge: when the game puts you near Ocean Beach early on, take the moment it offers instead of rushing the objective marker. It is flagged missable because a scripted early-game window, if walked past, may not be offered again in the same form; the point of no return is leaving the opening sequence without taking the cocktail moment. If you are already past it, revisit Ocean Beach in free roam and use the bar or cocktail interaction there, and keep an early save until this one is safely ticked.
trophies.sources: Official PlayStation trophy description; PSNProfiles — GTA VI Trophy Guide

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom, through the glass, in classic style. Get inside a showroom, take a vehicle and drive it out through the front rather than using the door like a customer. It is flagged missable on caution: if your only showroom visit is a scripted mission segment, that segment is the point of no return, so do the smash during the visit instead of planning to return. In free roam, any vehicle showroom with a car inside and glass frontage should give you the same chance; pick a sturdy car so the glass does not stop you dead.
trophies.sources: Official PlayStation trophy description; Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI PSN trophy list

trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Visit the Kolt and Associates bowling alley and bowl with a proper follow-through. This is an activity trophy in disguise: find the named alley, start the bowling activity and complete your throw or game as the alley intends. It pairs with the Master of None sweep, since bowling is exactly the sort of activity type that sweep wants sampled once. No score target appears in the description, so enjoy the game rather than resetting for perfection.
trophies.sources: Official PlayStation trophy description; PSNProfiles — GTA VI Trophy Guide

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.guide: This hidden trophy describes a partnership moment with mass appeal, which points at a shared scene between the two protagonists rather than a repeatable activity. It is flagged missable because a story scene, once played past, does not return; when the campaign gives the pair a public, crowd-facing moment together, stay in it and let it play out fully instead of skipping ahead. The point of no return is completing the story sequence that contains the moment. The chapter-boundary saves recommended throughout Phase 1 are your insurance if it does not pop when expected.
trophies.sources: Official PlayStation trophy description; Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI PSN trophy list

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.guide: Make choices, for better or worse; PlayStation tracks a count for this one, noted in community listings as running to 500. Choices are the one resource the campaign cannot give back, which is why this is flagged missable in spirit: a choice passed over in a one-time scene is a scene you must replay from a save to revisit. The practical method is to never skip a decision prompt, pick deliberately whenever the story or a stranger offers a branch, and keep those chapter-boundary saves so major branches can be revisited. Across a full playthrough plus Phase 2 strands, the count builds naturally if you engage with every prompt instead of rushing markers.
trophies.sources: Official PlayStation trophy description; PSNProfiles — GTA VI Trophy Guide; Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI PSN trophy list

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.guide: Second time's the charm: succeed at something on your second attempt after failing it once. The natural reading is a fail-then-succeed sequence inside an event the game tracks, which makes it missable in practice, because a perfect first-try run through the relevant event leaves nothing to charm the second time. When you fail a story attempt, a race start or a challenge run, do not reload instantly; retry it and succeed, and watch for this to pop. If it never does during the campaign, deliberately fail then succeed at a repeatable challenge in Phase 3. Keep early saves until it lands so a campaign version of the moment can be replayed if needed.
trophies.sources: Official PlayStation trophy description; PSNProfiles — GTA VI Trophy Guide

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.guide: Witness something strange, something that makes you ask what just happened. Leonida hides odd encounters off the beaten path, so explore at night, follow up rumours and investigate anything that looks deliberately out of place during the Phase 2 and 3 sweeps. It is flagged missable with caution: a one-off scripted oddity, if driven past, may not repeat, so when something weird starts happening, stop and witness it fully rather than speeding on. Exploration for the 52 areas gives you the coverage; curiosity gives you this trophy.
trophies.sources: Official PlayStation trophy description; Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI PSN trophy list

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Knock someone down with a melee drive-by, bowling them over as the name jokes. Ride or drive past a pedestrian or enemy at speed and strike them with a melee attack from the vehicle so the impact, not a bullet, does the work. A motorcycle makes the timing easier to judge than a car. Pick an isolated target away from heavy traffic and police attention, line up the pass, and swing as you draw level; a clean knockdown is what the trophy is watching for.
trophies.sources: Official PlayStation trophy description; PSNProfiles — GTA VI Trophy Guide

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Launder a total of 250,000 dollars of marked bills through your contacts. Marked bills come from robberies, so this trophy quietly rewards the whole crime loop in this list: vaults, trucks, shops and operations all feed the pile. Route every marked bill through your contacts rather than sitting on it, and check the running total whenever you bank a big job. It usually completes late, during Phase 4, once the silver vault robberies and the endgame earning are done, so do not force it early.
trophies.sources: Official PlayStation trophy description ($250,000); Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI PSN trophy list

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide: Spend a cumulative 100,000 dollars across all shops. Every legitimate purchase counts toward the same pot, so clothes, weapons, vehicle work and supplies all help. The efficient approach is to stop hoarding: buy the good gear as you go instead of saving everything for the garages, and this lands on its own by the endgame. If it is somehow still short in Phase 4, outfit both protagonists fully and restock every consumable; that shopping trip is also genuinely useful for the final clean-up.
trophies.sources: Official PlayStation trophy description ($100,000); PSNProfiles — GTA VI Trophy Guide

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide: Purchase all 8 garage properties. Garages are bought with earned cash, so this is an endgame purchase list: finish the high-paying robberies and laundering first, then sweep the property icons and buy every garage outright. Owning them all also gives your discovered vehicles somewhere to live, which supports the 100-vehicle tally. If one garage will not sell, progress the story or the relevant strand and return, since property availability often follows campaign progress.
trophies.sources: Official PlayStation trophy description; Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI PSN trophy list (8 garages)

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app. Whenever you take a vehicle you intend to keep, register it in the app straight away rather than abandoning it; ten registrations accumulate quickly once the habit forms. Pair this with Whip It Good, because registering usually means discovering, and with the garage purchases, which give registered vehicles a home. If the app asks for a specific vehicle type, vary what you bring it instead of registering near-duplicates of the same car.
trophies.sources: Official PlayStation trophy description (10 vehicles); PSNProfiles — GTA VI Trophy Guide
